notes: kb/Work/PB445.md LANDED. "Neither literal-1 nor literal-2 shall be zero-length literals" (cite.py --check 14.9.37.3 -> OK, Syntax rules 13). The predicate is the standard's own structural test, added to the ONE literal module as CobolLiteral.IsZeroLength: 3.178 defines a zero-length literal as an "alphanumeric, boolean, or national literal that contains zero characters" and 8.3.3.1 makes contiguous delimiters the spelling of one (both cite.py -> OK), so every format answers -- "", '', N"", B"", X"", NX"", BX"". It is deliberately NOT Decode(raw).Length == 0, which also answers true for an ill-formed hexadecimal literal and would report the wrong rule. A figurative constant is never zero-length (8.3.3.6.4 GR3 b, with 8.3.3.6.3 SR2 closing the ALL form) and a concatenation expression is zero-length exactly when every operand is (8.8.3.3 GR2 c 2). pb445-search-all-zero-length-literal is COBOL1966 at all four editions.
